faq.title: Questions
faq.lead: Can’t find your answer? Contact the team.

q1.a: A prediction market exchange on Solana. You trade Yes and No shares on questions about real-world events. When a market resolves, each winning share pays 1 USDC and each losing share pays nothing.

q2.a: A share trades between 0 and 1 USDC, and its price reads as the market’s estimate of the chance. A Yes share at 62¢ means the market puts the chance at about 62%.

q3.a: Sell your shares before the market closes, or hold them until it resolves and claim 1 USDC for each winning share. If a market is voided, each share pays 0.50 USDC. Claims go to your trading account, and you can withdraw USDC to your wallet from there.

q4.a: Your USDC and shares are held on-chain in a trading account tied to your wallet. Orders need your wallet’s signature, and so do withdrawals, which Sols Market also co-signs. Each market’s collateral sits in that market’s own vault.

q5.a: Each market publishes its resolution rules before trading starts, and the rules do not change while it is open. At launch, Sols Market resolvers check the outcome against those rules and sign the result, with no challenge period. A market whose outcome is unclear can be voided.

q6.a: Takers pay a trading fee and makers pay none. The fee is highest for prices near 50¢ and lower toward either end, and the order summary shows it before you sign. Sols Market pays the Solana network fees, and deposits, withdrawals and claims are free.
